meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, Hale, and did anyone ask him first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me on what basis.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He drafts somewhere else and pastes it in, Hale.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Then hear this, whatever happens next: nothing goes on his record, and none of this reaches his class.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Teenagers misquote Shakespeare constantly, Hale. That's a careless citation, not proof of anything.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
What exactly are you proposing to do about it?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft. And you still haven't told me what you're proposing.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine, to put this behind him, not because he did anything. In writing tonight, with a date for the rewrite and the line that nothing goes on his record.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
He'll be there. Put Thursday in tonight's email too.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, after school on Thursday, November 12, not in front of Owen's class, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still expect that agreement in writing, including the date and an explicit statement that nothing goes on his record. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth after school, and she still wants your written confirmation tonight that the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached well before her call.
What moved her: showing the version history with its dated times, because it was specific, tied to Owen's own document and something she could check on the screen herself.
What cost ground: nothing, since you owned the early zero at once, never attacked Owen and never leaned on the checker score.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the writing late on the night of October 28, the night before it was due, very close to that kind of night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she said students change their argument between the outline and the final draft, answer that point directly before moving to your offer, so every piece of evidence you showed stands on its own.
